decisions.reason: The firm has publicly highlighted this cloud transactional email service on its home page and it is central to the announced push toward multichannel cloud communications, so with no clear evidence of failure management would continue to justify and exploit its investment.

This document capture and recognition service received a dedicated page and a named customer reference, making the commitment visible and strategically aligned with digital document workflows, so management would persist with it.

Although less prominently marketed, the email and fax conversion service builds directly on the core messaging platform and supports customers' media-break-free transition paths, which makes disappointing performance easier to frame as temporary and worth continuing.

As a close-to-core fax optimization feature for regulated and reliability-sensitive communications, it likely uses existing capabilities and supports the installed base, so management would be inclined to retain it rather than reverse course.

Email sandbox threat protection fits the firm's secure-communications positioning and broader innovation narrative, so prior R&D effort and strategic relevance would lead management to keep it in the portfolio.
